req.title: Login rejects wrong password
req.statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect password.' error when the password hash comparison fails.

doc.reasoning: Two violations were reported: test[0] has kind=negative but heuristic=EP (EP is for equivalence partitioning which applies to both positive and negative, but the rule requires negative tests to use NEG heuristic); test[3] has kind=negative but heuristic=STC (STC is a state-transition heuristic, not a negative heuristic). Fix: change test[0] heuristic from EP to NEG, and change test[3] heuristic from STC to NEG. All other tests (test[1] positive/DT, test[2] boundary/BVA) are already passing and are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_login_wrong_password_shows_error
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows (user Rahul with password 'stone' exists)
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Incorrect username.'
trace: R-FLASKR-010: system shall render 'Incorrect password.' when hash comparison fails
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)",
               ('Rahul', generate_password_hash('stone')))
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_login_wrong_password_shows_error():
    r = client.post('/auth/login',
                    data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpassword'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect username.' not in r.data

test_login_wrong_password_shows_error()

tests.name: test_login_password_off_by_one_char_shows_error
preconditions: Database is initialised with user Ishaan whose password is 'stone'
actions: POST /auth/login with username='Ishaan' and password='ston' (one character shorter than correct password)
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Incorrect username.'
trace: R-FLASKR-010: even a password differing by one character must fail hash comparison and render 'Incorrect password.'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)",
               ('Ishaan', generate_password_hash('stone')))
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_login_password_off_by_one_char_shows_error():
    # 'ston' is 'stone' minus the last character — boundary BVA
    r = client.post('/auth/login',
                    data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'ston'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect username.' not in r.data
    # also verify case-variant is rejected (catches case-insensitive mutation)
    r2 = client.post('/auth/login',
                     data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'Stone'})
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r2.data

test_login_password_off_by_one_char_shows_error()

tests.name: test_login_wrong_password_does_not_redirect
preconditions: Database is initialised with user James whose password is 'river'
actions: POST /auth/login with username='James' and password='RIVER' (wrong case)
expected: HTTP 200 (stays on login page, no redirect to index)
Session does not contain user_id (user is not logged in)
trace: R-FLASKR-010: failed password check must not advance session state to logged-in
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)",
               ('James', generate_password_hash('river')))
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_login_wrong_password_does_not_redirect():
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    r = client.post('/auth/login',
                    data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'RIVER'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r.data
    # confirm session has no user_id — state did not advance
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess

test_login_wrong_password_does_not_redirect()
